findings.section: Behaviour contract › P2 — the kit's reports in Go
findings.summary: The order and source of the record and denial lines are only defined relative to the rows ('in folder order, then sequence order, as the rows'). When `vloop metrics` exits non-zero there are no rows, yet the brief says 'the rest of the block follows as usual'. internal/runs orders folders by their earliest record timestamp, not by name. So the kit must either reimplement that ordering or pick name order, and the brief does not say which.
findings.evidence: internal/runs/runs.go:190-210 (sortFolders: timestamp first, then path); the P2 sentence 'Record lines and denial lines come in folder order, then sequence order, as the rows', next to 'When it exits non-zero … the rest of the block follows as usual'. The failing fixture (most likely a bad iterations.jsonl line, which runs.Load rejects and report.py skips) also stops the kit from using runs.Load.
findings.fix: Pin it literally. For example: 'the kit reads the records itself; folders in name order, records in sequence order; fixtures name their folders in the order of their timestamps', or 'in by_session order from `vloop metrics <run id> --by session --json`, and in folder-name order when that command fails'. Also say where the denial lines come from when metrics fails: the kit applies P1's `text` rule to the records itself.

findings.section: Behaviour contract › P2 — the kit's reports in Go
findings.summary: The 'Session records: <n>, schema-valid <k> (<schema> <c>, …).' line has no literal form for a brief whose run folders hold no session file. An acceptance run that halts before the plan session's record is written produces that case.
findings.evidence: The P2 block defines the parenthesis only by its entries ('session/v3 2, session/v4 3', 'no schema <c>'). Nothing says whether n = 0 prints '()', drops the parenthesis, or prints something else.
findings.fix: Add one sentence, for example: 'with no record, the line is `Session records: 0.`'. Unsure whether any fixture will hit this; if none does, the sentence still keeps the program and the test from diverging.

decisions: Per-session view as `--by session` on `vloop metrics`, not a new `vloop sessions` command. Agree.

`by_session` added to metrics/v4 as an optional property, no v5. Agree. Not stated: close snapshots (.vloop/state/metrics/<run id>.json) written after B37 will carry by_session, including each denial's text (masked commands, already in the session records). The operator should know snapshots grow.
The kit as one Go program under tools/copilot-acceptance/kit/ run with `go run`, not a vloop subcommand, and no jq. Agree, following the tools/agent-eval precedent.
Byte-for-byte reproduction of the Python, gated on Python-made goldens that task 2's gate regenerates from the base. Agree; this is the strongest part of the brief.

The reports' own session tables replaced by `vloop metrics --by session`, plus a per-record self-schema check with per-version counts. This replaces the Python's check against the expected version (session/v3 for C5.1, v4 elsewhere): a record of the wrong version now shows in the counts but is not flagged INVALID. Acceptable, but it is a weaker check the operator should accept knowingly.

The denial `text` precedence (message, command, file_path, tool_input.command, tool_input.file_path). Agree; it matches the Claude, Copilot and shell-loop shapes (internal/driver/agent.go:200-213, agent_copilot.go:246-252).
Text-table conventions: `#` with three digits, credits `-` versus `0.00`, turns falling back to num_turns, `error` as yes or -. Fine.
The scripts make their dir argument absolute, with `mkdir -p`. As a side effect hook.sh now creates <dir> before it dies with 'run run.sh first'. Harmless.
Acceptance only at close on the real CLI (work.sh, run.sh, the B34 clone, a clean `git status --ignored`). Agree.
checked: facts (B36 real-data rows: 13 records, model opus/sonnet, 9m42s, $2.89, 1m38s, $0.30, denials 3+2+1+2=8, cost sum 5.6702516; internal/runs reader and folder order; metrics phase switch and Total; the --by refusals in internal/cli/metrics.go; export's delete of by_task; metrics.v4.json has no additionalProperties; report.py's six kinds and table shapes; hook.py's VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE, MODES and exit paths; bypass.sh's calls heredoc and perl; every script's dir/here/top/die order; the denial shapes the driver writes), consistency, rules (CLAUDE.md, the architect additions, BSD and git -C constraints, roadmap row present in the working tree), runnability (the go check after each task; testdata paths not ignored by .gitignore and outside the root-anchored .vloop fence; schema validate needs no repo root; a loop session has run python3 before (B24 T5))
